resources.string: Startup options
Restart to Windows, default system, boot menu
Restart to Windows
Start Windows once. The start-up after that follows the default system.
Restart to Windows now? The start-up logo will appear twice; this is normal.
Start by default
Android
Windows
Not known yet (restart once)
%1$s (takes effect at the next start-up)
Saved. It takes effect at the next start-up.
Restart to boot menu
Opens the boot menu (fastboot, other slot, other systems, factory reset). Volume keys move, the power key selects.
Restart to the boot menu now?
Could not do that (%1$s). Nothing was changed.
No startup options are available on this device right now.

When Windows is the default, restarting from Android still comes back to Android; only starting up after shutting down from Android goes to Windows. If, right after shutting down from Android, you pick another system in the boot menu, the next time you choose Android it may first go to Windows once.
Windows was not started
Android had something to finish first (for example a system update, or the last start-up did not complete), so this start-up went to Android. Please choose “Restart to Windows” again.
The default system was reset to Android

The boot menu had been set to always start one particular Android item, which stops automatic rollback from working. It was cleared and the default is Android again. To make Windows the default, use Startup options.
Windows replaced the boot menu

The start-up file that opens the boot menu is no longer the one Android installed (usually after a Windows update or repair). The computer may start straight into Windows. Use “Repair boot” in the Windows companion tool or the USB installer. Nothing was changed automatically.
